I have farmed in Iringa for many decades, and this small maize plot is intercropped with beans as it always has been. Because the rains have been reliable here in the Southern Highlands and I still have a bit of cash from selling potatoes last season, I will buy a small amount of fertilizer from the shop in town—just one small bag because money is tight and I must watch my costs. I also keep a few cattle, so I will spread manure on this plot before planting, and I will use improved seed since it grows well when paired with fertilizer. My sons and grandchildren will help with the digging and weeding, so we will manage the work ourselves without hiring labor, and we certainly do not irrigate here as we depend on the rains; I do not spray chemicals on maize because it is not worth the expense.
